title: Exodus: out of slavery, to God
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions and its rows of docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Exodus opens where Genesis ended. Jacob's family has become a nation, and the nation has become slaves.
The rescue doesn't begin with their faith. It begins with God's attention.
So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

scripture.text: So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

lines: The book has two halves. The first tells the rescue from Egypt and the road through the wilderness. The second takes place almost entirely at one mountain, Sinai.
Exodus gives as much space to where God will live as to how Israel got free.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the name of God
lines: The book turns on a name. At the bush, God tells Moses who he is.
Pharaoh begins by asking who the LORD is, that he should obey him. The plagues are sent so that Egypt and Israel will know.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the Passover and the sea
lines: Israel keeps the first Passover and goes free, on a night of great sadness in Egypt. At the sea, God makes a way.
This is the Old Testament's defining act of salvation. The rest of the Bible keeps coming back to it.

scripture.text: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: a law for rescued people
lines: Then comes the law, and the order matters. The laws aren't a ladder for earning God's favor. They're given to people he has already rescued.
In Hebrew, one word means both to serve as a slave and to serve God in worship. Exodus is a change of masters.

scripture.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: God comes to live with them
lines: The last third of the book is about a tent. The golden calf nearly ends that hope. Moses pleads for the people, and God renews the covenant.
And the book ends at the goal the whole story has been moving toward.
The glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

scripture.text: the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

lines: Start with chapter one. The key chapters are three, twelve, fourteen, nineteen, twenty, thirty-two, thirty-four, and forty.
And don't hurry through the tabernacle chapters. Their length is part of the point.
God didn't only bring his people out. He came to live with them.
